question: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hilton Young Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on the basis of the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The Hilton Young Commission was set up in 1926 to review the working of the Indian currency and to suggest changes for its stabilization and better management.
 
• The Commission's report led to the enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on April 1, 1935, as the central bank of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country, responsible for regulating the issue of banknotes, maintaining reserves to ensure monetary stability, and operating the currency and credit system of India.
 
• It was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• The institution is headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
 
 
 
• **Hilton Young Commission**
 
 
• The Hilton Young Commission, also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, was established in 1926.
 
• The Commission was chaired by Sir Edward Hilton Young.
 
• Its primary purpose was to examine the Indian currency system and to recommend measures for its stabilization and management.
 
• The Commission's recommendations were instrumental in the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, is the legislative framework that led to the creation of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• The Act was passed to constitute the Reserve Bank of India to regulate the issue of banknotes and the keeping of reserves to ensure monetary stability in India.
 
• It also aims to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• The Act came into force on April 1, 1935, which is when the RBI began its operations.
